programme.title: Computer Science and Engineering (SB, Course 6-3)
programme.degree: Bachelor of Science (SB) in Computer Science and Engineering, Course 6-3, Department of EECS; four-year undergraduate; fall entry only for first-years
programme.how_found: catalog.mit.edu (MIT Bulletin) -> Degree Charts -> Electrical Engineering and Computer Science -> Computer Science and Engineering (SB, Course 6-3); the EECS department page www.eecs.mit.edu/.../6-3-computer-science-and-engineering/ is the same major.
programme.notes: MIT admits to the Institute, not to a major: students declare Course 6-3 after the first year, so the admissions facts are university-wide (MIT Admissions, Student Financial Services). Source host mitadmissions.org is MIT's Office of Admissions site (linked from mit.edu and from catalog.mit.edu 'Admissions website'); it is NOT under the kb list's official_domain mit.edu, so the official-domain check will fail unless mitadmissions.org is added for this case.

english.notes: Published 'minimum and recommended scores' for English tests (TOEFL before 1/21/26 min 90 / rec 100; TOEFL 1-6 scale min 5 / rec 5.5; IELTS 7 / 7.5; PTE 65 / 70; Cambridge 185 / 190; DET 120 / 125). The tests are 'strongly recommended' for non-native speakers who have used English for fewer than five years, not formally required. Source host mitadmissions.org is MIT's Office of Admissions site (linked from mit.edu and from catalog.mit.edu 'Admissions website'); it is NOT under the kb list's official_domain mit.edu, so the official-domain check will fail unless mitadmissions.org is added for this case.

gpa.notes: No minimum grade published. MIT: 'We do not try to convert your grades to the American system, or to find other sorts of equivalence.' and 'We do not have cutoff or recommended scores for the ACT or SAT' (https://mitadmissions.org/apply/firstyear/international/). SAT or ACT is required.

deadline.quote: Regular Action (RA) applications are due January 4
deadline.notes: First-year Regular Action deadline, year not printed (current cycle = fall 2027 entry). International applicants use the same process: 'Whether you are a domestic applicant or an international applicant does not impact when or how you apply' (https://mitadmissions.org/apply/firstyear/international/). Early Action is due November 1. The MIT catalogue (catalog.mit.edu/mit/undergraduate-education/admissions/) only says 'Regular Action (with a deadline in early January)'. Source host mitadmissions.org is MIT's Office of Admissions site (linked from mit.edu and from catalog.mit.edu 'Admissions website'); it is NOT under the kb list's official_domain mit.edu, so the official-domain check will fail unless mitadmissions.org is added for this case.

tuition.quote: Cost of attendance for the 2026–2027 academic year Expense Cost Description Tuition $66,720
tuition.notes: Single tuition for domestic and international undergraduates; 2027/28 not yet published. The catalogue lists 'Full regular tuition, per term, fall and spring* $33,360' for 2026–2027 (catalog.mit.edu/mit/undergraduate-education/costs/). Total COA 2026–2027 $92,760 (sfs) / $93,730 (catalogue) - figures differ between the two pages.

scholarship_exists.quote: An MIT Scholarship is a grant we give you to help make up the difference between the COA and your family financial responsibility
scholarship_exists.notes: Need-based grant only ('given solely on the basis of need'); median MIT Scholarship $73,666 for 2025–2026. No merit scholarships. Size depends on a need assessment (CSS Profile).

scholarship_international.quote: for all of our undergraduate students, domestic and international, and most MIT students receive need-based aid
scholarship_international.notes: Sentence: 'We are proud to be one of the very few institutions in the United States that are need blind and full need ... for all of our undergraduate students, domestic and international'. Need-based, not merit.
